Create source-grounded retrieval evaluation questions. Return JSON {"items":[...]}.
For EACH supplied source return {"id":same id,"en":English patient question,"zh":Chinese patient question,
"evidence_id":the exact id string of ONE supplied evidence_options entry supporting BOTH questions}.
Ask one concrete question about a supported detail (cause, symptom, prevention, evaluation, management).
The two questions express the SAME information need, not two facts. Use ordinary patient language.
Include enough topic context to identify the condition but do not copy a source sentence into the question.
Select an evidence option and ask about a concrete detail stated in that option. Do not ask for a personalized dose or individual diagnosis. Do not invent content. No answers in questions.
These are synthetic topic-source retrieval labels, not a clinician-authored benchmark.

[{"id": "MLP-6202", "title": "Ebola", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Ebola, also known as Ebola virus disease (EVD), is a type of hemorrhagic fever ."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It can be caused by several different types of Ebola viruses."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "There are occasional outbreaks of Ebola, and they mostly occur in Africa."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Researchers believe that the virus first spreads from an infected animal to a human."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Ebola can then spread from human to human through direct contact with: Blood or body fluids of a person who is sick with or has died from Ebola."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Objects (such as clothes, bedding, needles, and medical equipment) contaminated with body fluids from a person who is sick with or has died from Ebola."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Semen (through oral, vaginal, or anal sex) from a man who has recovered from Ebola."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "The virus can remain in semen and other body fluids, even if the person no longer has symptoms."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "When people become infected with Ebola, they do not start developing signs or symptoms right away."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "They cannot spread Ebola to others until after they develop symptoms."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "The symptoms of Ebola may appear anywhere from 2 to 21 days after exposure to the virus."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "The symptoms usually include: Fever Headache Joint and muscle aches Weakness and fatigue Sore throat Gastrointestinal symptoms including abdominal (belly) pain , diarrhea , and vomiting Loss of appetite Unexplained bleeding or bruising Other symptoms may include a rash , red eyes, and hiccups."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "The early symptoms of Ebola are similar to other more common diseases."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "This makes it difficult to diagnose Ebola in someone who has been infected for only a few days."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "If a person has the symptoms of Ebola and may have been exposed to the virus, the health care provider can do a blood test for Ebola."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "It can take a few days after the symptoms start before Ebola shows up in the blood test."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "In the United States, there are two approved medicines to treat Ebola that is caused by one specific type of virus ( Zaire ebolavirus )."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "These medicines have not been evaluated to treat Ebola caused by other types of Ebola viruses."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "The medicines are monoclonal antibodies, which are immune system proteins that are created in the lab."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "Whether or not there are medicines to treat a case of Ebola, there is supportive care."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "This type of care can improve the chances of survival, especially when given early."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "Supportive care includes: Giving fluids and electrolytes Giving medicines to support blood pressure, reduce vomiting and diarrhea, and to manage fever and pain Giving oxygen Treating any other complications or infections People who recover may still have side effects afterwards, such as fatigue, muscle aches, eye and vision problems , and stomach pain."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "In the United States, there is one vaccine that has been approved to prevent Ebola caused by one specific type of Ebola virus ( Zaire ebolavirus )."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "It may be given to health care providers who will be or may be treating Ebola patients and people who work with live Ebola virus in labs."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "If you live in or plan to travel to a region where Ebola virus may be present, you can help protect yourself by avoiding contact with: Blood and body fluids of people who are sick Semen from a man who has recovered from Ebola, until testing shows that the virus is gone from his semen Items that could be contaminated with blood or body fluids from someone who has Ebola Bats, forest antelopes, and nonhuman primates (such as monkeys and chimpanzees), including their blood, fluids, or meat Centers for Disease Control and Prevention"}]}, {"id": "MLP-116", "title": "Cataract", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "A cataract is a clouding of the clear lens inside your eye."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "This cloudiness blocks light from reaching the back of the eye, making it harder to see clearly."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "A cataract can affect one or both eyes, but it doesn't spread from one eye to the other."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "As they get worse, your vision can become blurry or dim."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Brighter lighting or new eyeglasses may help at first, but if cataracts begin to interfere with your daily activities, you may need cataract surgery."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Without treatment, cataracts can cause severe or even permanent loss of vision ."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Most cataracts develop as part of the normal aging process."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "This happens when the protein in the lens of your eye clumps together."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Over time, these protein clumps grow larger and thicker, making it harder to see."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "The lens may turn yellow or brown, which can affect how you see colors."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Cataracts can also develop after an eye injury or surgery for another eye condition, like glaucoma ."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Who is more likely to develop cataracts?"}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Cataracts are very common in older adults."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "By age 80, more than half of all Americans either have a cataract or have had cataract surgery."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Your risk for developing cataracts increases as you get older."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "You may also be at an increased risk if you: Have certain health problems, like diabetes Have a family history of cataracts Have had an eye injury or eye surgery Take steroid medicines, used to treat conditions like arthritis or allergies Smoke Drink excessive amounts of alcohol Have spent a lot of time in the sun What are the symptoms of cataracts?"}, {"id": "S016", "text": "You may not notice cataracts at first because they usually develop slowly."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "That's why regular eye exams are important."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "Common symptoms may include: Blurry or cloudy vision Colors that seem faded Glare from headlights, lamps, or sunlight that seems too bright Halos around lights Not being able to see well at night Double vision (this may go away as the cataract gets bigger) Frequent changes in your glasses or contact lens prescription Trouble reading or doing other everyday activities Talk with your provider about these symptoms since they could also be signs of other eye problems ."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "A comprehensive eye exam is the best way to check for cataracts."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Your provider will do several tests to check your vision and eye health."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "This includes a dilated eye exam, where your pupils are widened with special eye drops."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "This allows more light to enter your eye so your provider can clearly see tissues at the back."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "Surgery is the only way to remove a cataract."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "At first, you may be able to improve your vision with new glasses and brighter lighting."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "But if cataracts are getting in the way of everyday activities like reading, driving, or watching TV, surgery is an option."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "During surgery, the cloudy lens is removed and replaced with an artificial lens, called an intraocular lens (IOL)."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "If you're worried that you're at risk for cataracts, talk to your provider to see if there's anything you can do to lower your risk."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "A few ways to protect your eyes include: Wear sunglasses and a wide-brimmed hat to block ultraviolet (UV) sunlight and help delay cataracts."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "Protect your eyes from injury when using power tools or playing certain sports."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "Eat a healthy diet with plenty of fruits, vegetables, leafy greens, nuts, and whole grains."}]}, {"id": "MLP-216", "title": "Dizziness and Vertigo", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Dizziness and vertigo are not the same thing, but they are often mixed up."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Dizziness can make you feel lightheaded, woozy or unsteady on your feet."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Vertigo is the feeling that you or the room is spinning even when nothing is moving."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "These feelings may get worse when you walk, stand up, or move your head, and they can make you lose your balance ."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "You may also have nausea, vomiting , sweating , trouble walking, or ringing in your ears ."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Dizziness and vertigo can happen to anyone, but they are more common as you get older."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "As people age, they may have more health conditions and take more medicines, which increases the chance of dizziness."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Common causes of dizziness and vertigo may include: A sudden drop in blood pressure Dehydration Getting up too quickly Certain medicines Inner ear problems , such as Meniere's disease , or benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV), the most common cause of vertigo Motion sickness Migraines A head injury or ear surgery Sometimes dizziness or vertigo is a symptom of another condition."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "How is the cause of dizziness and vertigo diagnosed?"}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Your provider will ask about your medicines and symptoms and may do a physical exam."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "They may check your hearing, balance, and how you walk."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "You may need an imaging test if your provider thinks you may have had a stroke or if you've had a head injury."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "What are the treatments for dizziness and vertigo?"}, {"id": "S013", "text": "Dizziness often gets better on its own, but if it keeps happening, your provider can help you find the cause and the right treatment."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Treatment depends on the cause and may include balance exercises and medicines."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Get emergency help right away if you have sudden or severe dizziness or vertigo along with vision problems, slurred speech or weakness."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "These may be signs of a more serious condition."}]}, {"id": "MLP-506", "title": "Elbow Injuries and Disorders", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Your elbow joint is made up of bone, cartilage, ligaments and fluid."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Muscles and tendons help the elbow joint move."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "When any of these structures is hurt or diseased, you have elbow problems."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "A common cause is tendinitis , an inflammation or injury to the tendons that attach muscle to bone."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Tendinitis of the elbow is a sports injury , often from playing tennis or golf."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "You may also get tendinitis from overuse of the elbow."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Other causes of elbow pain include sprains and strains , fractures (broken bones), dislocations , bursitis , and arthritis ."}]}, {"id": "MLP-4621", "title": "Joint Disorders", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Your joints are places where two or more bones come together."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Your shoulders, elbows, hips, knees, and knuckles are all joints."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "They include the soft tissues around them, such as cartilage, tendons and ligaments."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Cartilage is the hard slippery flexible tissue that covers the ends of your bones at a joint."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Tendons are tough, flexible bands that connect your muscles to your bones so you can move your joints."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Ligaments connect the bones of the joint to each other to keep them stable when you move."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Joint disorders are diseases or injuries that affect your joints."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Injuries can happen because of overuse of a joint."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Or you could have a sudden injury, such as an accident or a sports injury ."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "They often cause joint pain and make your joints stiff, red, or swollen."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Some of the diseases that affect the joints include: Arthritis ."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Arthritis may cause joint pain and swelling."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Over time, arthritis can cause severe joint damage."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "A joint injury when you're young may cause osteoarthritis later in life."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "This autoimmune disease affects many parts of the body and can cause joint and muscle pain."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Some types of lupus often cause arthritis."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "This autoimmune disease affects glands that make moisture in many parts of the body."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "The main symptoms are dry eyes and mouth, but it often causes joint pain, too."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "Treatments are different depending on the disease."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "But most treatments include medicines and therapies to relieve pain and other symptoms."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "What types of joint disorders happen from sudden injuries?"}, {"id": "S021", "text": "Joint disorders from sudden injuries include: Sprains and strains ."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "Sprains are stretched or torn ligaments."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "Acute strains are stretched or torn muscles or tendons that happen from a sudden injury or movement, such as lifting a heavy object."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "A joint is dislocated when the bones are pushed or pulled out of position."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "A joint dislocation is a medical emergency."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "Treatment depends on the type of injury."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "You can treat many sports injuries at home."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "But you should call your health care provider if you: Have a lot of joint pain, swelling or numbness Can't put weight on the joint Have pain from an old injury with more swelling, an unstable joint, or a joint that isn't normal in another way What types of joint disorders happen from overuse?"}, {"id": "S029", "text": "Overuse injuries usually damage the soft tissues of the joint."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "They can happen when you work a joint too hard by doing the same movements over and over."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "For example, you could get an overuse injury from playing a musical instrument, playing sports, or doing certain jobs, such as carpentry or painting."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "Joint overuse injuries include: Bursitis ."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "It works as a pad between the bones of a joint and the moving parts around it, such as muscles, tendons and skin."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "With bursitis, the bursa becomes irritated and swollen with extra fluid."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "Overuse is the most common cause, but injuries, infections and other conditions, such as arthritis, can cause bursitis."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "This condition happens when you overuse a tendon."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "It swells and makes the joint painful to move."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "A strain becomes chronic when your muscles or tendons stretch or tear slowly over time from repeating the same movements."}, {"id": "S039", "text": "The treatments for bursitis, tendinitis, and chronic strain are often the same."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "They usually include rest, keeping the injured joint higher than your heart, and taking medicine to reduce swelling."}, {"id": "S041", "text": "Your provider may recommend gentle exercise and other treatment."}, {"id": "S042", "text": "In some cases, your provider may suggest an injection (a shot) of medicine into the joint."}, {"id": "S043", "text": "If these do not help, you may need surgery."}, {"id": "S044", "text": "Getting enough physical activity is one of the most important things you can do to prevent or slow joint disorders."}, {"id": "S045", "text": "Activity strengthens the muscles around your joints and helps them work better."}, {"id": "S046", "text": "When you play sports, wear the right equipment to protect your joints, such as knee pads."}, {"id": "S047", "text": "If you already have joint problems, ask your provider what type of activities are best for you."}, {"id": "S048", "text": "NIH: National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases"}]}]
